clues: This resort city sits on the west bank of a big river mouth in south China. The small city of Macau lies just to its southeast.
Most rain here falls in two wet spells from April to October. Late spring brings damp air and rain, then summer storms bring typhoons and heavy rain.
In 1980, this city was named one of the first four special trade zones in China. That early pick made it stand out from the rest.
A big study in 2014 called this the most liveable city in all of China. Guests also rate it as a top tour spot in the land.
A long bridge from this city leads straight to Hong Kong. Macau sits just next door, on the same shore of the wide river mouth.
